summary: Missouri Conservation Commission steel tower in Miller County, erected 1950; sold at auction in 2013 and dismantled and moved on May 21, 2013.

facts.status_note: Dismantled and moved on May 21, 2013, per Central US Lookouts; no source describes the site now.

events.note: Steel tower erected on a 15.15-acre towersite acquired in fiscal 1950-51

evidence.supports: Missouri towers ranged from 60 to 120 feet tall; most made of steel
evidence.quote: Towers ranged from 60 to 120 feet tall
Most were made from steel, but early towers were made of wood.

evidence.supports: Wildfires spread unchecked before the commission was created in 1936
evidence.quote: Prior to the creation of the Missouri Conservation Commission in 1936, wildfires often spread uncontrolled across the Missouri Ozarks.

evidence.supports: Fire towers were the most effective method of fire detection for decades
evidence.quote: Fire towers were the most effective method of fire detection for decades.

evidence.supports: State conservation agency owned 15 fire towers in 1941
evidence.quote: In 1941, there were 15 towers owned by MDC.
In 1966, MDC operated 102 fire towers, and the U.S. Forest Service operated 43 in Missouri.

evidence.supports: Agency for the tower was the Missouri Conservation Commission

evidence.quote: FY 1950-51: A 15.15 acre towersite was acquired.
2013: Sold at auction for the sum of $2500.00.
May 21, 2013: The tower was dismantled and moved.

notes_for_editor: Only tower-specific source is the Central US Lookouts compilation, which quotes Missouri Conservation Commission annual reports without links. It gives no staffing, fire, sale-buyer or destination details. The 2013 sale and move dates are the only post-1950 events. anyplaceamerica.com and missourilife.com returned 403 and were not used. Brief access 'unknown' left unchanged; no source supports a level.
